entry.title: [BIP Draft] Signing message encoding
entry.summary:
A new draft Bitcoin Improvement Proposal (BIP) has emerged, evolving from discussions about payload exchanges between wallets and air-gapped signing devices in the context of miniscript. Initially, this effort focused on QR code-based communication, particularly for tasks such as retrieving extended public keys (xpubs), registering descriptors, verifying addresses, and signing Partially Signed Bitcoin Transactions (PSBTs). Over time, the specification broadened its scope beyond QR codes, aiming to standardize interactions with any form of external signer, whether the data transfer is achieved via QR, USB, NFC, or files.
The draft BIP now encapsulates comprehensive support for descriptors and miniscript, aligning with BIP-388 wallet policies to enhance compatibility and security. It integrates advanced features including MuSig2 multisignature protocols as outlined in [BIP-373](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0373.mediawiki), and silent payment functionalities described in [BIP-375](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0375.mediawiki). These additions aim to facilitate more robust, flexible, and privacy-preserving workflows for both developers and end-users interacting with external signers.
For those interested in reviewing or providing feedback, the draft proposal can be found at [this GitHub Pull Request](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/pull/2353), and further background and discussion are available in the [DelvingBitcoin forum post](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/qr-based-signing-flow-payloads-in-miniscript-context/2464). Community input is encouraged to ensure the proposal meets the diverse needs of wallet and hardware signer implementations within the broader Bitcoin ecosystem.
